RFC 8620 §7.3 push. Sends a `state` event (StateChange for Email, Mailbox and Thread) when the account's state moves: at once on new mail, otherwise noticed within 5 seconds. `ping` (seconds, 5 to 300; 0 for none), `closeafter=state`, `types`. At most 8 connections per account.

Upgrade with the `jmap` subprotocol (required). Text frames carry `Request` objects, answered with `Response` (or `RequestError`) carrying the same `requestId`; `WebSocketPushEnable` (optional `dataTypes`, `pushState`) starts `StateChange` pushes with `pushState`, `WebSocketPushDisable` stops them. Same login as /jmap/api/; an upgrade the session cookie authenticates must come from one of this site's pages (Origin), and Basic credentials are refused from another site's page. At most 8 push connections per account, shared with /jmap/eventsource/. Credentials come from the Authorization header or the session cookie only, never from the URL. Every 20 seconds the connection checks that what signed it in still works (the session, agent key or app password not revoked, the password unchanged, the account still there) and closes with 1008 when not. A request over maxSizeRequest or maxCallsInRequest gets the same error as over HTTP and the connection is closed with 1009.

X-Mailrs-Folder (from an export here) or X-Gmail-Labels (a Gmail Takeout) decides the folder and read state; Status: R marks a message read in any other mbox. Mail the user wrote is filed as a sent copy, the rest into the Inbox and then read and archived as the file says. Junk and Trash are skipped, and a Message-ID already in the mailbox is not filed twice, so an interrupted import can be run again. Nothing a delivery sets off runs: no filters, forwarding, webhooks or notifications. Received mail is judged by the fraud rules the receiver runs and held when they say so; the screening rules run in the mode they run in on arrival. Nothing is recorded about the senders.
